page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor, utilizing the arm64 architecture. The instance features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. This instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory performance, with a PassMark memory score in the top tier (top 10%) and uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths of 298.84 GB/sec and 132.09 GB/sec respectively, both placing in the strong category. Single-threaded and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speeds are also strong, reaching 13.85 GB/sec and 190.92 GB/sec. In contrast, CPU-bound tasks such as stress-ng single-core (1706.8) and multi-core (27291.47) performance fall into the average category. Large-model LLM inference represents a performance tradeoff, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model registering in the weak category at 31.21 tokens/sec, while text generation for the same model remains average at 17.01 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c8gn.4xlarge delivers high memory bandwidth and network throughput relative to its compute-optimized hardware class. The lack of bundled local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may affect workloads dependent on high-speed local disk I/O. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, high baseline network bandwidth, and strong database operation benchmarks (24214.69 on PassMark), this instance is suited for network-intensive applications, database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
